title: Interpretability
tagline: Probing, the residual stream, circuits, superposition, sparse features and steering
summary: What computations happen inside a language model? This course covers probing and attribution, the residual-stream view of Transformers, circuits such as induction heads, superposition, sparse dictionary learning of features, causal interventions and steering, and the open problems of understanding large models.

overview: Interpretability asks whether we understand what LLMs actually compute. This course covers circuits, superposition, causal effects, and mechanistic interpretability.
The key insight is that individual neurons are not interpretable in isolation. Circuits, not neurons, are the unit of interpretation.
outcomes: Explain mechanistic interpretability and circuit discovery.
Describe activation patching and causal mediation analysis.
